subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: The linked bug, this PR, and the competing open PR encode incompatible cron lifecycle semantics that affect existing persisted jobs, future defaults, and session-state retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a persisted-row or doctor/load repair path for existing omitted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only contract
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation direction after caller, UI, docs, and legacy recovery gaps are handled.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the default only for newly normalized jobs and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a persisted-row or doctor/load repair path for existing omitted jobs while preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans cron defaults, persisted SQLite behavior, and compatibility policy, and steipete has the strongest recent history across those files.
